title: Make / made / made
subtitle: make dinner, make a mistake, it makes me feel ...
summary: Use make for food and drink, for mistakes, noise and appointments, and to say how something makes you feel.

lesson.heading: Make food and drink
lesson.text: We **make** food and hot drinks. The past form is **made**.

examples.text: I **make** breakfast for the family every day.

lesson.heading: Other things you make
lesson.text: We also **make** a film, a video or a photocopy - things that did not exist before you started.

examples.text: She's **making** a film about her city.
They're **making** a video of the wedding.
He's **making** a photocopy of the letter.

lesson.heading: It makes me (feel) ...
lesson.text: Use **make someone (feel) + adjective** to say how a thing changes how you feel. The word *feel* is not necessary.

examples.text: Going by train always **makes me (feel) tired**.
My friend called me stupid. It **made me (feel) angry**.
That meal was horrible. It **made me feel sick**.

lesson.heading: Expressions with make
rows: I made a mistake in the exercise.
I want to make an appointment with the doctor.
When I get up I make my bed.
The children are making a noise.
They are making a mess in the living room!
I love your new dress - you made a good choice.
lesson.note: Make an appointment means fix a time to see somebody.

left.label: Say make
examples: I **made a mistake** in the exercise.

right.label: Not make - use do or take

lesson.text: Keep two lists in your notebook, one headed make and one headed do, and add every new expression you meet.

exercises.prompt: I always ___ a lot of mistakes when I speak English.
exercises.explanation: We make a mistake, not do a mistake.

exercises.prompt: Our neighbours had a party last night. They ___ a lot of noise.
exercises.explanation: The past of make is made. We make a noise.

exercises.prompt: I am ___ dinner for my parents this evening.
exercises.explanation: We make breakfast, lunch and dinner.

exercises.prompt: What do you think, the silver car or the white one? We must ___ our choice today.
I ___ an appointment with the doctor for you. It's at 5 o'clock.
exercises.explanation: We make an appointment when we fix a time to see someone.

exercises.prompt: That film about the war made me feel ___.
exercises.explanation: Something makes you feel sad, happy, tired, angry or sick.

exercises.prompt: Match each situation with the way it makes you feel.

exercises.statement: I have to make my homework before dinner.
exercises.explanation: I have to do my homework before dinner. We do homework.

exercises.statement: Can I make a photo of you?
exercises.explanation: Can I take a photo of you? We take a photo.

exercises.statement: He's 25 but he never makes his own washing.
exercises.explanation: He's 25 but he never does his own washing. We do the washing.

exercises.prompt: Do we say make or do with each of these?
The children are very loud this evening. Say it.
exercises.answer: The little boys are making a noise.

exercises.prompt: Going by train always ___ me feel tired.
exercises.explanation: Something makes you feel tired, happy or sad.
